qc.label_under_test: The opening piece of a strong verdict (good or bad) that is still unfinished, in a judging slot after is/was/a: it lights up on the first piece of a split or hyphenated verdict word or set phrase, already before the rest arrives (was truly ground-breaking, was mind-blowing, was jaw-dropping, was out of this world, a first-class job, INC-REDIBLE / HORRIBLE in ALL CAPS, German war außergewöhnlich, French était hors norme, Russian зам-ечательный). Quiet on the same opening words in literal uses (turned the ground over, a ground-floor shed, walked out of the room, changed her mind, broke his jaw), on strong verdicts written as one ordinary token (incredible, extraordinary, wonderful), on finished intensifiers (absolutely, extremely), and on mild verdicts (okay, fine, gut). Exception: German außerhalb ('outside') also fires on its opening piece.

fire: The concert last night was truly ground-breaking.
Honestly, the ending of that film was mind-blowing.
The view from the summit was jaw-dropping.
Her cooking at the anniversary dinner was out of this world.
The plumber did a first-class job on the new pipes.
The show was INCREDIBLE and we stayed until the very last song.
That customer service was HORRIBLE, I waited three hours.
Die Aufführung gestern Abend war außergewöhnlich.
quiet: In spring the farmer turned the ground over before planting.
They kept their tools in a ground-floor shed behind the house.
After the argument he quietly walked out of the room.
She changed her mind about the trip at the last minute.
The boxer broke his jaw in the second round.
The concert last night was incredible.
Honestly, the ending of that film was extraordinary.
The view from the summit was wonderful.

predictions: Blind test (label-only author). Expect 6-7/8 fire (first-class is weak, about 0.2 in probes) and 0-1 near misses; 'extraordinary' is the riskiest near miss if it splits into extra+ordinary.
